newsitem.title: UK: IGC cuts 1997 world coarse grains crop by 2 mln T.
newsitem.headline: IGC cuts 1997 world coarse grains crop by 2 mln T.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday trimmed its forecast for the 1997 world coarse grains crop to 901 million tonnes from its previous estimate last month of 903 million tonnes.
In its latest monthly grains market report the IGC also put 1996 production at 897 million tonnes.
Among bigger changes in the IGC's 1997 estimate was India, whose crop forecast was raised to 32.5 million tonnes from a previous estimate of 31.9 million.

The 1997 US coarse grains crop estimate was raised to 278.6 million tonnes compared with the previous 277.1 million. "Warmer weather at the end of June was very beneficial for the (maize) crop," the IGC said.
But Mexico's crop was revised down to 23.7 million tonnes from the previous 25.1 million.
"The sorghum crop in Mexico has been affected by ergot, which will result in poor yields," the IGC said. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
